title: The Maggid's circle
hookLine: the Maggid of Mezeritch taught a circle of students who carried Hasidism across Eastern Europe

cards: Someone asks a Hasid what Torah he learned from his teacher. His answer, as Hasidim tell it: I didn't go to hear him teach Torah. I went to see how he laces and unlaces his boots.
It sounds like a joke. It isn't. Not the lecture, but the way a person lives, down to the laces, can be the lesson.
That teacher was the Maggid of Mezeritch, and the students who sat in his house would carry Hasidism across Eastern Europe.

teach.b: Rabbi Dov Ber was called the Maggid: the preacher, the one who tells. A serious scholar, he came to the Baal Shem Tov, the tradition says, as something of a skeptic, and left as his disciple.
After the Baal Shem Tov died, as the tradition tells it, the Maggid became the center of the movement. He wasn't a traveler.
He was often ill, and he taught from his home in the small town of Mezeritch, in what is now Ukraine. But the students who came to him were extraordinary.
Shneur Zalman of Liadi, who would found Chabad. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, the defense attorney. Zusya of Anipoli, who worried about not being Zusya, and his brother Elimelech of Lizhensk.
Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, who later led a group of Hasidim to the Land of Israel. And many more. When the Maggid died, something unusual happened.
There was no single heir. His students went out across Eastern Europe, and each became a teacher in his own place.

One circle in one house turned into many Hasidic communities, each with its own melodies and customs. The opening mishnah of Pirkei Avot includes the charge: raise up many disciples. The Maggid did exactly that.
His teaching went out the door, in the boots of his students.

how: Many Hasidic communities trace their lineage back through their founding rebbe to the Maggid of Mezeritch and the Baal Shem Tov, and they retell the Maggid's teachings at gatherings and on the anniversary of his death.

practice: Of everything you've heard this year, a story, a word, a saying, a practice, let the one that has stayed with you come to mind, and think of one person who might need it.
Not as a lecture: the way the Maggid's students carried him, by how they lived. If you pray, give thanks for whoever taught you.

wordCard.voice: Maggid, meaning preacher, the one who tells. Dov Ber of Mezeritch's students went home after his death and carried Hasidism across Eastern Europe.

orig.note: Hebrew: preacher, one who tells. From the root that also gives Haggadah, the telling.

carryVoice: Your line: pass it on. One small house in Mezeritch became many communities. See you tomorrow.
